title: Eyelet border baby blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket with an all-over eyelet border frame in DK on 4 mm needles.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket with a five-stitch eyelet-row border on all four sides and a stocking-stitch centre, worked in DK on 4 mm needles. The eyelet rows are worked horizontally in the cast-on and cast-off rows and vertically as a five-stitch side border on every RS row. About 255 g of DK.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 5th series (1889), §Knitted Nursery Squares with Eyelet Borders, gives a cot blanket with running eyelet side borders and top-and-bottom eyelet rows as a standard Victorian nursery knitting pattern.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles, unblocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A decorative frame of small holes worked around the perimeter of a flat piece. The horizontal borders (cast-on and cast-off rows) are worked as eyelet rows that replace a plain knit row. The vertical side borders are worked as a running five-stitch eyelet column on every RS row: k2, yo, k2tog, then the body, then k2tog, yo, k2 on the other side.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 4 mm needles. A five-stitch
eyelet border
runs on all four sides. The centre is stocking stitch. Finished size: 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. The eyelet border was chosen to frame the stocking-stitch centre without the bulk of a garter border. The horizontal eyelet rows at cast-on and cast-off and the running vertical columns at each side edge all use the same yarn-over and k2tog technique. The blanket requires wet blocking to prevent the stocking-stitch centre from curling, but the eyelet borders stabilise the edges considerably. Budget about 255 g (about 560 m / 615 yards) of machine-washable DK.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 255 g (about 560 m / 615 yards) of DK-weight machine-washable yarn. Smooth DK shows eyelets clearly.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

items.name: Blocking mat and pins
items.qty: Strongly recommended, stocking stitch centre curls without blocking

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. The eyelet columns at the sides are slightly narrower than the same stitch count in stocking stitch.
At 20 stitches per 10 cm with 165 stitches, the blanket will be about 83 cm wide.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 165 stitches. Long-tail tail: (4 × 165) / 10 + 15 = 66 + 15 = 81 cm. Measure 95 cm of tail.
Bottom eyelet rows
Rows 1 to 4: knit all stitches (garter base for the eyelet row).
Row 5 (eyelet row, RS): k2, *yo, k2tog; repeat from * to last st, k1.
Rows 6 to 8: knit all stitches.
Body with side eyelet columns
RS rows: k2, yo, k2tog, k to last 5 sts, ssk, yo, k3.
WS rows: k3, p to last 3 sts, k3.
Continue body rows until the blanket measures 83 cm from the cast-on edge.
Top eyelet rows
Work 4 rows all knit, then 1 eyelet row (row 5 above), then 4 more rows all knit. Total added length: about 7 cm. Final blanket length: 90 cm.
Stitch count check-ins

At row 135 (about 45 cm): count across. You should have 165 stitches. Eyelet rows never change stitch count because each yo pairs with a k2tog. At row 268 (about 89.5 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults
Stocking-stitch centre curling inward at the sides: the side eyelet columns are worked correctly but the blanket has not been blocked yet. Block firmly after washing.

Eyelet column appearing as a solid rib column: the yo was placed after the k2tog on a WS row, yo placements only occur on RS rows in this pattern. WS rows are plain purl in the centre and garter at the edges.
Cast-off
Cast off knitwise on the last garter row with a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in ends. Wet block firmly: soak the blanket, squeeze out water, pin to measurements on a blocking mat, allow to dry fully. The stocking-stitch centre will lie flat after blocking.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry, reshaping to measurements each time.
What to try next

From an eyelet-bordered stocking-stitch blanket, the progression is a lace panel blanket where the eyelet columns extend across the full width in a repeating pattern. The same yarn-over and k2tog technique applies throughout.
